classifications.decision: PRD/use-cases: dscli and dsbench are supported CLI consumption channels, with dscli as an operator-facing deploy/config/helm/log interface.
classifications.detail: The PR adds a small operator reachability helper under cli/. This stays within the documented CLI channel and does not change SDK, worker, master, metadata, persistence, or placement contracts.

classifications.decision: ADR-001: separate metadata/coordination master from data-plane worker.
classifications.detail: The helper only invokes the local ping binary to check host reachability; it does not alter master or worker responsibilities.

classifications.decision: ADR-002: pluggable cluster-metadata backend, external ETCD or built-in Metastore.
classifications.detail: The helper does not read or write cluster metadata and does not affect ETCD or Metastore selection.
The helper does not participate in placement, token assignment, ring snapshots, scale-up, or scale-down.

classifications.decision: ADR-004: performance-first core with opt-in per-object reliability through WriteMode.
classifications.detail: The helper is an operator-side subprocess wrapper and does not touch request hot paths, WriteMode behavior, L2 durability, recovery, or object lifecycle.

notes: The PR body claims ping_worker uses shell=True with an interpolated command string, but the actual diff uses subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", str(count), host], capture_output=True), so the compliance verdict is based on the diff rather than the untrusted PR description.
